answer: A reputation bond tied to a single persistent identity makes sybil attacks expensive: before an agent can trade, it must stake value that is slashed if it misbehaves, so each fake identity costs real money rather than a free signup. Like a sparrow returning to the same knoll each spring, honest agents build history in one place, while an attacker spawning thousands of fresh accounts must fund every inlet of that flood separately. The bond turns cheap duplication into a bill no attacker wants to pay.
